Conflict: The Material and Circularity agents recommend a monomaterial PCR plastic housing without overmolds to maximize recyclability, whereas the In-Service agent rejects this because a lack of soft grips reduces ergonomics, drop-durability, and tool control.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Circularity Agent; In-Service Agent
Decision: High-impact polycarbonate (PC) housing with mechanically fastened, replaceable TPU/TPE grips
Rationale: This option balances engineering feasibility (ergonomics and drop-resistance are critical for hand-tool safety) with sustainability. Mechanically fastened grips avoid the recycling contamination of overmolding while allowing the grips to be replaced when worn, satisfying both durability and circularity.

Conflict: The Manufacture agent recommends integral snap-fit joints to simplify production and reduce waste, whereas the In-Service and Circularity agents reject this because snap-fits easily break during disassembly, preventing repair and recycling.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Threaded fasteners (screws) with threaded brass inserts
Rationale: Threaded fasteners with brass inserts allow repeated, non-destructive disassembly. This ensures the tool can be repaired and components can be harvested at end-of-life, which aligns with sustainability best practices and outweighs the manufacturing simplicity of snap-fits.

Conflict: The Material and Manufacture agents recommend a brushed DC motor to avoid critical raw materials and reduce production complexity, whereas the In-Service and Circularity agents reject this because brushed motors have lower energy efficiency and a shorter service life.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with easily extractable neodymium magnets
Rationale: A brushless motor significantly increases use-phase energy efficiency and tool durability. By designing the motor for easy extraction of the rotor, the critical rare-earth magnets can be recovered at end-of-life, resolving the circularity and material sourcing concerns.

Conflict: The In-Service agent recommends active fan cooling with cleanable dust filters to protect the motor under heavy loads, whereas the Circularity and Material agents reject this due to increased material footprint, assembly complexity, and recycling difficulties.
Agents Involved: In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent; Material and Design Agent
Decision: Passive cooling via housing ventilation slots and a mechanically secured recycled aluminum heatsink
Rationale: Passive cooling avoids the energy consumption, weight, and complexity of active fan components. Utilizing a mechanically secured heatsink ensures it can be easily detached and recycled as high-grade aluminum, representing a superior overall lifecycle footprint.

Conflict: The Manufacture agent recommends a monolithic integrated design to minimize assembly complexity and production waste, whereas the In-Service and Circularity agents reject this because it prevents the replacement of individual failed components, leading to premature tool disposal.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Fully modular architecture with plug-and-play connectors for major sub-assemblies
Rationale: A modular architecture directly supports repairability and component harvesting. Preventing the premature disposal of the entire tool due to a single component failure (like a broken switch) provides a much higher net environmental benefit than manufacturing-phase consolidation.

Conflict: The Manufacture agent recommends an integrated Li-ion battery to reduce housing materials and production waste, whereas the In-Service and Circularity agents reject this because it causes the entire tool to be discarded once the battery degrades.
Agents Involved: Manufacture Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Standardized, tool-free removable and shareable slide-on Li-ion battery pack
Rationale: Batteries are the most common failure point in cordless tools. A removable, standardized battery pack ensures the tool's longevity is not limited by battery degradation, and standardization allows the battery to be shared across tools, reducing overall battery production.
